title: EEG: Three armed bandit gambling task
description: EEG recordings from 23 healthy college students performing a three-armed bandit gambling task with oscillating reward probabilities. Each stimulus slowly shifts between low and high reinforcement probability in different phases, making the task suited to studying reward processing, reward prediction error, and novel task-set generation. Corrugator EMG and skin conductance were also collected for most participants.
methods_description: Data were collected in 2014 at the Cognitive Rhythms and Computation Lab, University of New Mexico. Participants completed a Matlab-based three-armed bandit task in which reinforcement probabilities for each stimulus oscillated between 20% and 90% over many trials. Corrugator EMG and skin conductance were recorded for most participants, though quality was noted as dubious. Preprocessing scripts are included in the code folder.
